faq.question: Do I have to register if I own just one rental?
faq.answer: Yes, if you do not live in the building. One- and two-unit non-owner-occupied rentals register with the municipal clerk; buildings of three or more units register with the DCA. Without registration you cannot obtain an eviction judgment.

faq.question: Can I decline an applicant who pays with a Section 8 voucher?
faq.answer: No. Lawful source of income is a protected category under the NJ Law Against Discrimination. You may apply your normal, uniformly applied screening criteria, but you may not reject an application because it relies on a voucher, or advertise a unit as unavailable to voucher holders.

faq.question: Is the tenant ever responsible for repairs?
faq.answer: Tenants are responsible for damage they or their guests cause beyond normal wear and tear. Everything required to keep the unit habitable — heat, water, structure, systems — remains the landlord's duty. If keeping up with these obligations from a distance is the hard part, that is the job a property manager exists to do.
